liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help on the Way** (2 reviews): The opening Help, Slipknot, Franklin's and Music Never Stopped run is played very tightly; Help and Slipknot start a bit shaky and imperfect, but the band settles by Franklin's Tower [11][13]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): A return to the Franklin's lyrics prompts someone onstage to whoop in response to Jerry's solo; The transition from Franklin's Tower into Music Never Stopped is singled out as one of the best [14][21]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy is called picture perfect and is the reviewer's likely favorite of the night [11]
- **High Time** (1 review): High Time is extremely emotional, with Jerry's vocal sounding especially heartfelt through the second set [13]

## The recordings

- **gd76-06-19.prefm.unknown.12077.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): pre-FM broadcast master; 28 songs; 196 min; rated 4.17/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound weak on low end, with nothing coming through the subwoofer channel; Decent sound but light on bass; Phil is audible yet not forward, making the mix feel distant; Static blip cuts off the end of Cosmic Charlie [12][14][15][18][20]
- **gd1976-06-19.fm-sbd.seff.1859.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 169 min [2]
- **gd1976-06-19.prefm.nickspicks.10186.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 21 songs; 176 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1976-06-19.143275.fm.glassberg.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 21 songs; 181 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Small static bursts in Set II were in the broadcast itself; they have been removed; Station identifications have been removed from this version [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer feels the Capitol Theater seemed to bring out peak performances from the band [11]
- Reviewer attended, watching from several spots in the hall, and recalls Jerry and Bob communicating with each other onstage [17]
- Solid, but less energetic than earlier shows on the same tour, such as June 9th, 1976 [12]
- Reviewer says this is among the first of a string of shows, lasting almost four years, where the band is consistently on [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-06-19.prefm.unknown.12077.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer holds an FM source covering only Let It Grow through Goin' Down the Road, put on a metal cassette; Pre-FM source: soundboard master reel transferred to DAT, then to CD twice; seeder unknown [1][18]
- **gd1976-06-19.fm-sbd.seff.1859.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Jon Seff; source: FM > ? > DAT [2]. Also: FM soundboard source has no fades except at set starts and ends; split to keep jams together [2]
- **gd1976-06-19.prefm.nickspicks.10186.shnf**: transferred by Nick Georges; source: SBD master reel > DAT > CD (x2) > EAC (secure) > SHN (non seekable) [3]. Also: Pre-FM discs obtained in a trade with Mike French, who was asked for pre-1977 rarities; Tapes-in-circulation list describes this as a live broadcast of about 180 minutes, missing the encore [3]
- **gd1976-06-19.143275.fm.glassberg.warburton.smith.sirmick.flac2496**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Jimmy Warburton and Matt Smith and Sirmick; source: WNEW FM > Teac A3300 7.5 ips Dolby > Master Reel (Scotch Classic 3600 10,5) > Teac A3300 > Reel 1 @3.75 ips (Maxell UD35-90) - Recorded by Barry Glassberg,… [4]. Also: Source is an FM broadcast carried by WOUR Utica and WNEW New York [4]
